description:
We are a team representing London South Bank University Ajman. 

United by the belief that technology must be a force for global good, we are tackling the "Field Shift" challenge to support our most vital community: Farmers. Our project leverages NASA’s Earth observation data to help agriculture adapt to a rapidly changing climate. By translating complex environmental data into accessible, actionable insights, our goal is to empower farmers to make resilient, sustainable planting decisions that protect their livelihoods and secure our future food supply.
summary: EcoRotate is a comprehensive agricultural decision-support web platform created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, bringing together essential planning and earth-observation tools in one unified workspace. Its core features include an interactive map visualizer for pinpointing, drawing, and managing custom field boundaries, alongside detailed satellite data overlays that track vegetation health (NDVI) and soil moisture indices. The platform also offers a localized, multi-season crop rotation planner complete with tailored planting schedules, crop compatibility insights, and soil-preservation recommendations. Rounding out the user experience are clear visual analytics, a modern dark-mode interface, and full multilingual support designed for accessibility across diverse farming communities.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Field Shift (EcoRotate) is a multilingual agricultural decision-support web platform designed to translate open-access NASA Earth observation data into practical, localized crop rotation plans.

Users begin by locating their farmland on an interactive map visualizer and drawing custom field boundaries. Once a plot is selected, the platform overlays key satellite remote-sensing indicators, including Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) for crop health and soil moisture indices, alongside regional climate and soil profiles. Using these spatial and environmental inputs, the platform's recommendation engine generates tailored, multi-season crop rotation schedules that alternate nutrient-depleting crops with soil-restoring varieties (such as nitrogen-fixing legumes) suited to the plot's exact conditions.

Field Shift (EcoRotate) - Current Deployment

  • Current Architecture (Vercel Frontend): Field Shift currently runs as a fast, client-side web application hosted on Vercel, delivering instant access with zero server overhead for the NASA Space Apps demo.
    • Core Features: Mapbox-powered interactive field boundary selection, visual overlays for vegetation health (NDVI) and soil moisture indices, a multi-season crop rotation planner, dark-mode UI, and multilingual support.
    • Frontend Stack: Built with React, Vite, JavaScript/TypeScript, and the Mapbox API, using pre-processed NASA Earth observation datasets and client-side agronomic logic served over Vercel's global edge CDN.

Field Shift (EcoRotate) - Future Roadmap & Accessibility Improvements

To move beyond the current Vercel-hosted web prototype and reach every agricultural community worldwide, future development for Field Shift focuses on bridging the offline digital divide alongside full-stack backend expansion:

  • Direct-to-Phone AI Voice Helpline (100% Offline Accessibility):
    • How It Works: Field Shift's backend will connect directly to a telecom and cloud telephony provider (using real-time voice gateways linked to a FastAPI server). Any farmer can dial a dedicated phone number from a basic feature phone or landline, speak naturally with a multilingual AI assistant, and receive instant spoken crop-rotation recommendations tailored to their location and growing season.
    • Why It Matters: Roughly 80% of farmers globally either lack reliable internet access or do not have the digital familiarity required to navigate websites. Replacing screen-and-internet dependencies with a standard voice call ensures that farmers in remote, rural, and underserved regions can access NASA-informed agronomic guidance with zero technical barriers.
    • Transition from a client-only frontend to a decoupled backend powered by Python (FastAPI) for AI orchestration, speech-to-text/text-to-speech voice pipelines, and geospatial analytics, paired with Java (Spring Boot) for core service management.
    • Integrate automated ingestion of live NASA Earth observation feeds (such as NDVI vegetation health and soil moisture datasets) backed by a spatial database, allowing both web users and phone callers to build multi-season farm histories and receive timely planting alerts.
